target_customer: Hospitals and health systems that need patients to follow pre- and post-procedure instructions
problem: Patients miss or misread procedure instructions, causing cancellations and failed preparation.

founders.name: Adeel Yang
founders.background_notes: YC page says he is a physician.

technical_complexity.rationale: Scheduled text and email journeys tied to appointment data, with EHR integration work, are standard engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Hospital workflow integration creates some stickiness but messaging vendors were many by 2019.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Philips bought it in July 2019 to complement its VitalHealth and diagnostic offerings, and renamed the product Philips Patient Management.

market_need_then: A 2018 UCSF program using the product was linked to a 37.3% reduction in canceled or rescheduled prostate biopsies, and Brigham and Women's used it for colonoscopy prep.

rebrands.why: Product renamed after the Philips acquisition per one outlet.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself; it was folded into the Philips brand within weeks of acquisition.

outcome_analysis: Medumo sold patient instruction automation to hospitals, produced clinical results at UCSF and Brigham and Women's, and was acquired by Philips in July 2019 for an undisclosed amount. A physician founder with a prior acquired startup and measurable cancellation reductions supported the sale. Funding is not verified so capital efficiency cannot be judged.
notes: medumo.com did not resolve from this environment. Aggregators list a $2M to $2.1M seed (Dec 2017 to Jan 2018) with Cantos Ventures, YC and MassChallenge; unverified single-aggregator figures so no round recorded. Philips release says founded 2013; one source says 2017. CareTours as earlier product name is single-source. Competitor Twistle is from a March 2019 article, later than the batch; as_of reflects that. Twistle appears only in a March 2019 article, over a year after the batch, so it is excluded from the founding list.
